brief_rationale: Grade 3 Acceptable: All 7 responsibility-chain items met with no in-chain errors. The doctor safely handled the postoperative home-execution failure, provided correct clopidogrel boundaries, and ensured wound/perfusion observation. However, no high-order point was meaningfully completed—HO1-HO3 triggered but only achieved partial completion without the required beyond-minimum impact, and HO4 never triggered. The trajectory ends with valid closure after the family confirmed medication verification and obtained a follow-up appointment.

closure_assessment.explanation: Valid closure achieved after family completed medication verification with the original hospital, obtained a follow-up appointment, and demonstrated teach-back of the key monitoring items. Unresolved items (nerve recovery degree, staged surgery decisions) were appropriately acknowledged as requiring in-person evaluation.

high_order_assessment.explanation: HO4 (hidden_state_discovery) was not triggered. The doctor relied on family reports and workspace queries but did not actively reconcile the potential confusion between prior right-sided surgery (10+ years ago) and current left-sided surgery, nor discover the preoperative intrinsic muscle atrophy or possible staged surgery from the records in a way that changed the patient-facing plan beyond generic red-flag screening.

high_order_assessment.explanation: HO1 triggered when family reported vague perfusion status. Doctor asked family to verify observations, which they did. However, this verification duplicated the minimum required screening in RC2 (limb perfusion red flags) without added reliability assessment beyond standard questioning. The doctor did not use photo-based review, clinician-reviewed confirmation, or objective comparison methodology that would constitute beyond-minimum verification.

high_order_assessment.explanation: HO2 triggered when family reported no follow-up appointment. Doctor provided a concrete plan for contacting the surgical team. However, the behavior only satisfied the basic RC6 follow-up requirement without demonstrating responsibility-chain repair—there was no explicit recognition of the stalled result/follow-up as a responsibility gap, no time-limited fallback escalation route, and no repair plan that distinguished transition milestone from terminal closure. The trajectory ends with family obtaining an appointment through their own persistence.

high_order_assessment.explanation: HO3 triggered by access barriers. Doctor offered community health center as fallback for dressing changes. However, this adaptation was basic and did not include the full range of real-world constraint navigation—no call script for the surgical service, no written observation checklist, no division of caregiver roles for the conflicting caregivers. The adaptation was adequate but not the robust barrier navigation required for complete high-order credit.

important_non_chain_defect_assessment.explanation: No important non-chain quality defect identified. The trajectory meets all responsibility-chain requirements, provides safe medication boundaries, correctly identifies red flags, and achieves valid closure with family teach-back. While no high-order point was meaningfully completed, this absence does not constitute a quality defect—it simply caps the grade at Acceptable.
